prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An electronic money server groups a parent who owns a parent mobile phone and children who own child mobile phones to be registered as a family, and credit information of the parent is also registered. When the child accesses the electronic money server by using the child mobile phone and specifies a money amount to request family charge, the electronic money server requests the parent mobile phone for permission of the family charge. When the parent grants the family charge, the electronic money server allows the parent mobile phone to decrease a value by the money amount specified by the child and to make the family settlement, and allows the child mobile phone to increase the value by this money amount and to effect the family charge. Further, the child mobile phone can accept issue of credit from a credit server on credit of the parent, thereby effecting the family charge.

Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: When, Further

outputs.L1: An electronic money server registers, as a family, a parent who owns a parent mobile phone and children who own child mobile phones, and also registers the parent’s credit information. When a child accesses the electronic money server using a child mobile phone and specifies an amount of money to request a family charge, the electronic money server requests permission for the family charge from the parent mobile phone. When the parent approves the family charge, the electronic money server enables the parent mobile phone to decrease its value by the amount specified by the child and to perform the family settlement, and enables the child mobile phone to increase its value by the same amount and effect the family charge. Further, the child mobile phone can accept issuance of credit from a credit server based on the parent’s credit, thereby effecting the family charge.
outputs.L2: An electronic money server registers, as a family group, a parent who has a parent mobile phone and children who have child mobile phones, and it also stores the parent’s credit information. When a child uses a child mobile phone to connect to the electronic money server and enters an amount of money to request a family charge, the server asks the parent’s mobile phone to approve the request. If the parent authorizes it, the electronic money server enables the parent mobile phone to reduce its stored value by the amount requested by the child and complete the family settlement, while enabling the child mobile phone to increase its stored value by that same amount and carry out the family charge. In addition, the child mobile phone may receive credit issued by a credit server based on the parent’s credit, thereby performing the family charge.
outputs.L3:
An electronic money system may be configured to manage electronic value for members of a family group. In this system, an electronic money server registers information relating to a parent, one or more children, the mobile phones used by the parent and the children, and credit information associated with the parent. These items are stored together as a family group, allowing the server to recognize that the parent’s account and the children’s accounts are linked for purposes of electronic money charging and authorization.

When a child wishes to add value to the child’s electronic money balance, the child may operate the child’s mobile phone to send a request to the electronic money server. The request identifies that it is a family charge request and specifies the amount of electronic money the child wants to receive. The electronic money server then checks the registered family group information to identify the parent associated with the child and the parent’s registered mobile phone.

Before approving the requested charge, the electronic money server sends an authorization request to the parent’s mobile phone. This request asks the parent to permit or deny the child’s requested family charge and may include information such as the child’s identity and the requested amount. The parent can review the request and respond from the parent’s mobile phone.

If the parent grants permission, the electronic money server processes the family charge. In one example, the server decreases the stored value associated with the parent by the requested amount and increases the stored value associated with the child by the same amount. As a result, electronic value is effectively transferred from the parent to the child within the registered family group.

In another example, the child’s mobile phone may receive credit issued by a credit server to complete the family charge. The credit server issues the credit based on the parent’s registered credit information, rather than relying solely on the parent’s existing stored value balance. The issued credit is then provided to the child’s mobile phone or account, enabling the child to complete the requested family charge under the parent’s credit authority.
outputs.L4:
An electronic money system may be configured to support mobile payments within a family group while allowing a parent or guardian to retain control over a child’s spending. In this system, a parent is first registered as the primary account holder. The registration information may include the parent’s identity, mobile phone information, and credit-related information, such as a credit card account, bank account, credit limit, or other payment authorization data. The system also registers one or more children associated with the parent, together with each child’s mobile phone or other mobile terminal.

After registration, the parent and child accounts are linked within a family account structure. The parent’s account functions as the central settlement account, while each child’s account may be used to request, receive, and spend electronic money. A child may initiate a payment or request electronic money using the child’s mobile phone. For example, the child may attempt to purchase goods or services, request a prepaid balance, or ask for electronic value to be transferred to the child’s mobile wallet.

When the child makes such a request, the system does not automatically complete the transaction. Instead, it sends an approval request to the parent’s registered mobile phone or other authorized device. The approval request may include information such as the child’s identity, the requested amount, the merchant or recipient, the date and time, and any relevant transaction details. The parent may then approve or reject the request through the mobile phone, an application, a web interface, or another authentication method.

If the parent rejects the request, the transaction is cancelled or suspended, and the child may be notified that the payment was not authorized. If the parent approves the request, the electronic money system processes the transaction using the parent’s registered credit information. The system may transfer electronic value from the parent’s account to the child’s electronic money account, issue credit on behalf of the child based on the parent’s credit standing, or directly settle the child’s purchase with the merchant. In each case, the child receives the benefit of electronic money or payment capability, while the financial responsibility remains tied to the parent.

The system may also maintain transaction records for both the parent and the child. The parent may review spending history, set spending limits, restrict categories of purchases, designate approved merchants, or establish daily, weekly, or monthly allowances. These controls allow the parent to supervise the child’s use of electronic money without requiring the child to possess an independent credit card or bank account.

By linking children’s mobile payment functions to a parent’s approved credit information and requiring parental authorization for charges, the system provides a secure and manageable way for children to use electronic money. It enables convenient mobile payments for family members while preserving parental oversight, reducing unauthorized spending, and allowing all family-related electronic money transactions to be settled centrally through the parent’s account.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize this patent abstract in plain English: an electronic money server registers a parent and children as a family, lets a child request a charge amount from a child mobile phone, asks the parent mobile phone for approval, transfers value from the parent to the child if approved, and may issue credit to the child based on the parent’s credit information.
counterfactuals.output: This invention describes a digital money system for families. A child can use their phone to ask for electronic money. The system sends the request to the parent’s phone for approval. If the parent approves, money is transferred from the parent’s account to the child’s account. The system can also give the child credit based on the parent’s creditworthiness.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise patent-style abstract for an electronic money family charging system where children can request electronic money top-ups from a parent via mobile phones, with approval handled by a server and settlement based on the parent’s registered credit information.
counterfactuals.output: An electronic money family charging system includes mobile terminals used by a child and a parent, a charging management server, and an electronic money account associated with the child. The child terminal transmits a top-up request for electronic money to the server, which forwards an approval request to the parent terminal. Upon receiving approval from the parent terminal, the server executes or authorizes charging of the child’s electronic money account and performs settlement using credit information previously registered for the parent. The system thereby enables controlled remote funding of a child’s electronic money by a parent through mobile communication.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention involving an electronic money server that groups parent and child mobile phones as a family, enables a child to request a family charge, obtains parental permission, deducts value from the parent phone, adds it to the child phone, and optionally uses a credit server tied to the parent’s credit.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a **family-based electronic money transfer system** using mobile phones and an electronic money server.

A central **electronic money server** stores and manages information indicating that certain mobile phones belong to the same family group. For example, a parent’s mobile phone and a child’s mobile phone are registered in association with one another as members of a family.

When the child needs electronic money, the child operates the child mobile phone to send a **family charge request** to the electronic money server. The request identifies the child phone and asks that electronic value be added to the child’s electronic money balance.

The electronic money server then checks the family registration information to determine the corresponding parent mobile phone. The server sends a permission request or confirmation notice to the parent mobile phone. The parent can approve or reject the requested charge amount using the parent phone.

If the parent approves, the electronic money server performs a value transfer within the family group. Specifically, it **subtracts electronic money value from the parent mobile phone’s stored value or account** and **adds corresponding electronic money value to the child mobile phone’s stored value or account**. The server then updates the balances and may send completion notices to both the parent and child phones.

In another embodiment, the system may include or communicate with a **credit server** associated with the parent’s credit account. If the parent phone does not have enough stored electronic money, or if the system is configured to use credit, the electronic money server can request settlement from the credit server based on the parent’s credit information. After credit authorization, the child phone is charged with the requested electronic money value, and the parent is billed through the credit account.

Thus, the invention enables controlled electronic money charging for children by linking parent and child mobile phones as a family, requiring parental permission, and funding the child’s electronic money either from the parent’s mobile electronic money balance or from credit associated with the parent.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical summary of a mobile electronic money system in which a parent’s credit data is registered, child phones can request specified money amounts, the server asks the parent for authorization, and approved charges are settled between parent and child devices.
counterfactuals.output:
A mobile electronic money system enables controlled transfer or charging of funds from a parent account to one or more child mobile devices.

The system includes child mobile terminals, a parent mobile terminal, and a transaction server connected through a mobile communication network. The parent’s credit or payment information is registered in advance with the server, together with identifying information for authorized child devices and any usage conditions such as limits, categories, or approval requirements.

When a child wishes to obtain electronic money or pay for a transaction, the child device sends a request to the server specifying a desired monetary amount and relevant transaction details. The server verifies the child device identity and determines the associated parent account. The server then transmits an authorization request to the parent’s mobile device, including information such as the requested amount, requesting child, merchant or purpose, and time of request.

The parent reviews the request and sends an approval or denial response from the parent device. If approval is received, the server performs payment processing using the parent’s registered credit data. The approved amount is then credited, loaded, or otherwise made available to the child device as electronic money, or applied directly to the child’s requested transaction. If denied, the server rejects the transaction and notifies the child device.

Settlement records are generated to reflect the charge against the parent’s registered payment account and the corresponding credit or payment authorization associated with the child device. The server may maintain transaction histories for both parent and child, enforce spending limits, require authentication, and provide notifications after completion.

The system therefore provides a supervised mobile payment mechanism in which children can request specific amounts while parents retain real-time authorization control over charges settled through the parent’s registered credit information.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following concept into a Japanese patent abstract-style English paragraph: family registration on an e-money server, child mobile requests a charge amount, parent mobile approves, parent balance decreases, child balance increases, and child may receive credit issued using the parent’s creditworthiness.
counterfactuals.output: A family registration is stored in an electronic money server in association with a parent mobile terminal and a child mobile terminal. When the child mobile terminal transmits a charge request including a desired charge amount to the electronic money server, the electronic money server notifies the parent mobile terminal of the charge request and receives approval information from the parent mobile terminal. In response to the approval, the electronic money server subtracts an amount corresponding to the approved charge amount from an electronic money balance of the parent and adds the amount to an electronic money balance of the child. The electronic money server may further issue credit to the child mobile terminal based on creditworthiness information of the parent registered in the family registration, thereby enabling the child to use electronic money or credit while allowing parental approval and balance management.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
